parts.title: Melting Ice
parts.text: On Monday, the science teacher showed photos of a **glacier** that had shrunk by half in forty years. Nadir stared at the bare gray rock where thick ice used to be. "Temperatures **fluctuate** from year to year," he argued. "Maybe this is just a normal cycle." The teacher smiled and handed Alma a slab of stone holding the imprint of a **fossil** fern. Millions of years ago, she explained, warm swamps covered this region, proving that Earth's climate has changed before. "But never this quickly," she added.

parts.title: Digging for Causes
parts.text: Jules drew a diagram on the board. "Certain gases trap heat the way glass does in a **greenhouse**," he said. Alma raised her hand. "Isn't the hole in the **ozone** layer a separate problem?" The teacher nodded. That thin shield high in the sky blocks harmful sunlight, and a worldwide ban on certain chemicals had helped it begin healing. Proof, she said, that people can fix things. Smoke from cars and factories adds each **pollutant** to the air, and coal and oil are **finite**, so someday they will run out. If nothing changes, the results could be **catastrophic**, with flooded coastlines and failed crops.

parts.title: Building Answers
parts.text: "Can we **avert** the worst?" Jules asked. For their project, the trio built a paper **turbine** that spun whenever Nadir blew on it. "Wind and sunshine are free," Alma said. "The hard part is learning to **harness** them." Nadir calculated that solar panels on the school roof were a **viable** plan that would pay for themselves in nine years.

parts.title: The Change of Mind
parts.text: That evening, Nadir realized his argument had melted away like the ice in the photographs. Facts had changed his mind, and now his job was to help change others.
